hypothesis: Storing the weights in S3 One Zone-IA instead of S3 Standard does not change weight-download time or init latency: One Zone-IA is a cheaper storage class with the same first-byte latency and throughput, not a performance tier. It adds a $0.01/GB retrieval fee on every cold start and snapshot init.

changed_variable.name: weight object storage class
changed_variable.held_fixed: same general-purpose bucket, same GGUF bytes (S3 full-object SHA-256 = 8dbb8872...), same loader code path (HEAD + 32 x 64 MiB ranged GETs into a memfd), same function zip 26eb2651..., configuration and pinned runtime

conclusion: No change (pre-registered rule). Cold weight_download p50: Standard 24.99 s, One Zone-IA 25.03 s; ratio 1.0016, bootstrap 95% CI [0.9978, 1.0054], inside the +/-2% band (n=50 each, 79 MiB/s both). The primary bootstrap treats the 50 concurrent cold starts per arm as independent; a paired round-cluster bootstrap over the 5 rounds (sensitivity only) gives [0.9972, 1.0067], also inside the band. Within the dominant CPU part 0xd40 (84 of 100 cold starts) the ratio is 0.9995 [0.997, 1.0051], round-cluster [0.9973, 1.0072], also no-change; cold download time does not depend on the CPU part here (pooled medians 24.85 / 24.97 / 25.15 s on 0xd0c / 0xd40 / 0xd4f). Snapshot-init download 0.9998 [0.995, 1.011]. Cold first request total 35.93 vs 35.95 s, Restore Duration 3.22 vs 3.21 s, warm inference 0.66 vs 0.66 s. Intervals that exclude 1.0: cold probe forward (aggregate 1.0109 [1.0012, 1.0136]; 0xd40 1.008 [1.0019, 1.0131], +1.9 ms on weights already in memory, plus a CPU-mix effect in the aggregate), and CPU part 0xd4f cold weight_download 1.0049 [1.0017, 1.009] / throughput 0.9949 [0.9912, 0.9987] on n=6 per arm drawn from different rounds, a +0.5% low-n signal inside the band that this run cannot separate from round timing. Host: the handler recorded the /proc/cpuinfo CPU part per environment (0xd0c, 0xd40, 0xd4f; one part per environment, both arms drawn in near-equal mix); implementer, HWCAPs, cgroup limits and kernel were not recorded and no processor generation is claimed. 1,200 invocations, 0 errors, 0 class mismatches, 1,200/1,200 answers bit-identical to the P1 reference, and the same answer SHA-256 on both arms. Cost is the only material effect. One Zone-IA charges $0.0208 per download ($20.80 per 1,000 cold starts or snapshot inits), against $0.000013 for Standard and $0.0012 at Express One Zone list prices. It saves $0.027 per month in storage on this 2.08 GB object, so it breaks even at 1.3 downloads per month and has a 30-day minimum. Restores read no S3 bytes. This run cost $3.64 at list prices. Recommendation: keep the weights in S3 Standard.
